description: High-occupancy COOPERATIVE tridiagonalization for the n=1024 dense shapes (shape 7 mixed1024 b60, the holdout big shape at the ~106ms cuSOLVER floor): the measured root cause is that cuSOLVER's tridiag is memory-bound BECAUSE only 60 matrices underfill the 148 SMs (low occupancy), and its ~50ms per-call fixed floor punishes any batch split. Mechanism: assign MANY CTAs per matrix (cooperative reduction across SMs) so all 148 SMs are busy from just 60 matrices, doing a one-stage blocked Householder full->tridiagonal (NO band intermediate, so no serial bulge-chase) with the trailing symmetric rank-2 update as a cooperative batched GEMM, then feed the tridiagonal to a batched stedc/D&C solve + back-transform. Targets occupancy / memory-throughput / insufficient-parallelism; keep the residual gate + cuSOLVER fallback, route guarded per shape.

t1: cooperative blocked-Householder tridiag (torch-level LAPACK sytrd/latrd) on whole b60 batch, trailing rank-2b update as batched 3xTF32 GEMM per panel (nb=32, 32 panels), Sturm/twisted tridiag solve + compact-WY back-transform, per-matrix residual gate. CORRECT (nbad=0/60, orth 3.4e-4<<9.2e-3 gate, eigr 9.2e-4<<1.8e-2). But shape7 106662->815169us (7.6x REGRESSION), geomean 27919->32498. Warm stage breakdown (probe): coop_tridiag 521-676ms (DOMINATES; matvec prec fp32/tf32/3xtf32 = 521/531/676ms, trailing prec ~neutral 521 vs 531) + tridiag_eigh(Triton Sturm/twisted) 101ms + backtransform 30ms, vs cuSOLVER whole-eigh 105ms. Root cause: the latrd PANEL REDUCTION (~1024 dependent per-column batched matvecs p=A@v + 2 correction GEMMs each, Python-launched) is the wall -- NOT the trailing GEMM (trailing prec neutral). This is the SAME memory-bound per-column symv chain cuSOLVER runs, but torch's unfused per-matvec is ~10x slower than cuSOLVER's fused symv. ncu (this brief) showed cuSOLVER's symv is ALREADY 88% occupancy at grid(64,60)=3840 CTAs -- so the wall is latency of the dependent chain, not low occupancy. 39/39 valid, no 'stream', -O3.

t2: matvec fp32 (not 3xTF32), trailing tf32, DBG off. shape7 815169->663755us (still 6.2x REGRESSION vs parent 106662), geomean 32498->31997. The fp32 matvec killed the 3xTF32 GEMV elementwise storm (t1 nsys: 26% CUDAFunctor_add x7559, 24% s64x64tf32 x3066) -> 815->664ms, but the FUNDAMENTAL wall persists: the latrd panel reduction is ~520ms (nb sweep 16/32/64/128 = 533/527/527/521ms, ~FLAT -> trailing GEMM negligible, latrd dominates) + tridiag_eigh(Triton) ~101ms + backtransform ~30ms. Root cause CONFIRMED: ~1024 dependent per-column matvecs p=A@v + 2 deferred-update correction GEMMs each, Python-launched (torch cannot fuse the per-column ops). cuSOLVER runs the SAME blocked latrd (latrd_trans_kernel/latrd_compute_w_kernel in parent nsys) in FUSED CUDA kernels at 88% occupancy -> ~10x faster per column. 39/39 valid, no 'stream', -O3.

t3: COOPERATIVE IN-KERNEL variant -- route n=1024 through the C-CTA cluster tridiag (mega_eigh_clust_split, C=5 -> 60x5=300 CTAs). shape7 106662->227728us (2.1x REGRESSION), geomean 27919->29481. Kernel itself 158ms (probe) / ncu 146.9ms; the extra ~70ms in benchmark is the orth-gate cuSOLVER fallback (orth_max 1.001 > gate -> the dense matrices fall back, each adding a ~50ms cuSOLVER-fragment floor per brief-88). DECISIVE ncu on mega_eigh_clust_split_k (grid (300,1,1)x(512)): Achieved Occupancy 25.0% (16 warps/SM) -- LOWER than cuSOLVER's symv 88% -- capped at Block Limit Shared Mem=1 (C=5 packed-FP16 half-triangle ~205KB/CTA -> only 1 CTA/SM). DRAM 0.24%, Compute(SM) 10.05% -- the kernel does almost NO memory OR compute work: 85.1% 'No Eligible' warps (0.17 eligible/scheduler of 4), issues 1 inst/6.7cy, and 73.9% of stall cycles are CTA-BARRIER stalls (19.9cy/inst waiting at the per-column cl.sync/syncthreads, ~1022 columns). This CONFIRMS the brief's fallback outcome: the cross-CTA grid-sync barrier cost per column DOMINATES and occupancy is WORSE than cuSOLVER, not better -- the many-CTA-per-matrix occupancy win is NOT realizable at n=1024 because (a) the big SMEM footprint caps CTAs/SM at 1 and (b) the serial per-column reduction forces ~1022 cross-CTA barriers. 39/39 valid, no 'stream', -O3.

t4 KEEPER: gate coop OFF (_COOP_ENABLED=False) -- both realizations regress n=1024, so shape 7 falls through to cuSOLVER (no regression). Machinery present+wired. shape7=106527us (==parent 106662, noise), shape4=46257, shape10=91927, shape12=30625 (all ==parent), geomean=27837 (==parent 27919, within noise). NO regression on any shape, 39/39 valid, no 'stream', -O3. This mirrors brief-88's economics-gated keeper: the cooperative tridiag (blocked-torch _eigh_coop + in-kernel-cluster _eigh_coop_cluster, both per-matrix residual-gated) is built, dispatched, and OFF because measured slower. DECISIVE MAP of the brief's lever: (1) cuSOLVER's tridiag is NOT low-occupancy -- ncu shows its symv at 88% occupancy (grid (64,60)=3840 CTAs, 55% SM/26% DRAM), latency-bound on the ~768-symv+2338-gemvx dependent chain; (2) torch-blocked cooperative panel = 664ms (launch/elementwise-bound: ~1024 per-column matvecs, each a batched GEMV torch cannot fuse; nb 16-128 flat -> trailing GEMM negligible); (3) in-kernel C-CTA cluster cooperative tridiag = 147ms kernel / 228ms w/ gate-fallback, ncu 25% occupancy (LOWER than cuSOLVER; Block Limit Shared Mem=1, C=5 packed-FP16 ~205KB/CTA -> 1 CTA/SM), 73.9% CTA-BARRIER stalls (19.9cy/inst at ~1022 per-column cl.sync), 0.24% DRAM/10% SM -- pure barrier-waiting. The many-CTA-per-matrix occupancy win is UNREALIZABLE at n=1024/b60: big-SMEM caps CTAs/SM at 1 (occupancy DROPS to 25%) and the serial per-column reduction forces ~1022 cross-CTA barriers that dominate. cuSOLVER's fused latrd (latrd_trans/compute_w kernels, 88% occ) is already near-optimal for this shape.

Built BOTH cooperative-tridiag realizations the brief named and mapped the lever with the ncu occupancy numbers the brief required. Parent shape7=106662us=raw FP32 cuSOLVER floor; final KEEPER (08d8b5689) gates coop OFF -> shape7=106527us, geomean 27837 == parent 27919 (NO regression on ANY shape, 39/39 valid, no 'stream', -O3). The coop machinery (torch-blocked _eigh_coop + in-kernel-cluster _eigh_coop_cluster, both per-matrix residual-gated + cuSOLVER fallback) is present, dispatched, and OFF because measured slower -- mirrors brief-88's economics-gated keeper.

KEY REFUTATION OF THE BRIEF'S PREMISE (ncu, this brief): cuSOLVER's tridiag is NOT low-occupancy. ncu on cuds_symv_lo_direct_kernel (shape7): grid (64,60) = 64 CTAs/matrix x 60 matrices = 3840 CTAs, Achieved Occupancy 88.3% (56.5 warps/SM), 55% SM / 26% DRAM. cuSOLVER already runs the blocked latrd cooperatively (latrd_trans_kernel/latrd_compute_w_kernel in nsys) in FUSED kernels at high occupancy. The wall is the LATENCY of the ~768-symv + 2338-gemvx dependent chain (each ~67us), NOT low occupancy.

TRIAL MAP (all shape7 vs cuSOLVER 106.7ms): t1 torch-blocked coop, 3xTF32 matvec = 815ms (nsys: 26% CUDAFunctor_add x7559 + 24% s64x64tf32 x3066 = 3xTF32 GEMV elementwise storm). t2 fp32 matvec + tf32 trailing = 664ms; nb sweep 16/32/64/128 = 533/527/527/521ms FLAT -> the trailing rank-2b GEMM is NEGLIGIBLE, the latrd panel reduction (~1024 dependent per-column batched matvecs p=A@v + 2 deferred-update correction GEMMs each, all Python-launched and unfusable) is the ~520ms wall. t3 in-kernel C-CTA cluster tridiag (mega_eigh_clust_split, C=5 -> 60x5=300 CTAs) = 147ms kernel / 228ms with gate-fallback; ncu DECISIVE: Achieved Occupancy 25.0% (LOWER than cuSOLVER's 88%!), capped Block Limit Shared Mem=1 (C=5 packed-FP16 half-triangle ~205KB/CTA -> only 1 CTA/SM), 0.24% DRAM / 10% SM, 85.1% 'No Eligible' warps, 73.9% of stall cycles are CTA-BARRIER stalls (19.9 cy/inst waiting at ~1022 per-column cl.sync/syncthreads). PER-PANEL(column) GRID-SYNC COST vs GEMM COST: the kernel is ~pure barrier-waiting (0.24% DRAM + 10% SM = ~90% idle on sync), so the cross-CTA sync EATS the entire budget -- exactly the brief's fallback outcome. C sweep: kernel arrays cap C<=8 (AhP[8]); C=10/12 -> illegal address.

WHY THE OCCUPANCY WIN IS UNREALIZABLE at n=1024/b60: (a) a full-n=1024 packed-FP16 triangle needs C>=5 CTAs to fit SMEM, and ~205KB/CTA caps residency at 1 CTA/SM -> occupancy DROPS to 25% (worse than cuSOLVER); (b) the serial per-column Householder reduction forces ~1022 cross-CTA barriers whose latency dominates. More CTAs/matrix shrink per-CTA SMEM but INCREASE cluster-barrier cost and don't reduce the ~1022 barrier COUNT.

OPEN DIRECTIONS I did NOT build (surfaced for the manager): (1) a BLOCKED IN-KERNEL latrd cooperative kernel that syncs once PER PANEL (~n/nb=32 grid.syncs) instead of per column (~1022) AND keeps A in GLOBAL (not SMEM) so occupancy isn't SMEM-capped -- the panel trailing update as an in-kernel WMMA GEMM; this is the only variant that attacks BOTH measured walls at once, but it is a large from-scratch cooperative-groups kernel and cuSOLVER's fused latrd at 88% occupancy is a high bar. (2) feeding the coop tridiagonal (d,e) to cuSOLVER's BATCHED stedc instead of the Triton Sturm/twisted (101ms) -- cheap but won't flip the 520ms reduction wall. (3) a hybrid that reduces ONLY the dense subset's columns -- but that fragments the batch (brief-88's mapped per-call floor). Given the ncu evidence that cuSOLVER's tridiag is already 88%-occupancy fused, and both cooperative realizations are barrier/launch-bound and LOWER-occupancy, the manager should weigh whether a from-scratch panel-grid-sync kernel is worth a follow-up vs the n=512 shapes where custom paths already win. The keeper preserves the machinery so re-enabling is one flag flip if a faster reduction primitive lands.
